docs.text: About CASTLE The CASTLE Lab weekly meetings are a place for students who are interested in computing related topics to socialize and share knowledge outside of the classroom, and to join extracurricular projects and events related to computing (and computer science). The CASTLE Lab is also open for students to use during the day as a social and work space. We hope to see you at our next meeting! Acronym CASTLE stands for the Computer And Software Teaching-Learning Experience.

docs.text: CASTLE Lab Printing Setup Overview The CASTLE Lab uses a centralized printing setup. The Lexmark printer is connected directly to the server lux using USB. The server runs CUPS and shares the printer with the Debian lab computers. The lab computers do not connect directly to the printer. Instead, they send print jobs to lux , and lux sends the jobs to the Lexmark printer over USB. Architecture: Lab Computer | | IPP / CUPS v lux.alfred.edu | | USB v Lexmark MS310/MS312 Series The shared printer is named: LabPrinter The FreeIPA server and print server are both: lux.alfred.edu The server currently uses the static IP: 149.84.129.206 1. Server-Side Setup All commands in this section are run on: lux.alfred.edu 1.1 Install CUPS Install CUPS and the CUPS client utilities: sudo apt update sudo apt install cups cups-client Enable and start CUPS: sudo systemctl enable --now cups Verify: systemctl status cups 2. Verify the USB Printer The Lexmark printer is physically connected to lux using USB. Check that Linux sees the printer: lsusb The printer appeared as: Lexmark International, Inc. Lexmark MS312dn To find the CUPS device URI: sudo /usr/sbin/lpinfo -v The Lexmark USB URI was: usb://Lexmark/MS310%20Series?serial=45147GLM3V8KL The model may display as MS310 Series even though the physical printer is an MS312dn. 3. Find an Available Printer Driver The Lexmark is connected over USB, so the CUPS everywhere driver cannot be used directly. Running: sudo /usr/sbin/lpinfo -m | grep -Ei 'Lexmark|MS310|MS312|Generic.*PostScript' returned: drv:///sample.drv/generic.ppd Generic PostScript Printer The Lexmark supports PostScript, so the Generic PostScript driver was used. 4. Create LabPrinter on lux Create the printer: sudo lpadmin \ -p LabPrinter \ -E \ -v 'usb://Lexmark/MS310%20Series?serial=45147GLM3V8KL' \ -m drv:///sample.drv/generic.ppd CUPS may display: Printer drivers are deprecated and will stop working in a future version of CUPS. This is a warning about future CUPS versions. It does not mean the current configuration failed. Set LabPrinter as the server default: sudo lpadmin -d LabPrinter Verify: lpstat -t The important lines should include: system default destination: LabPrinter device for LabPrinter: usb://Lexmark/MS310%20Series?serial=45147GLM3V8KL printer LabPrinter is idle 5. Test Printing Directly from lux Send a simple test job: echo "CASTLE Lexmark printer test" | lp -d LabPrinter CUPS should return a request ID similar to: request id is LabPrinter-1 Verify that the page physically prints. 6. Share LabPrinter Mark the printer as shared: sudo lpadmin -p LabPrinter -o printer-is-shared=true Enable printer sharing globally: sudo cupsctl --share-printers Restart CUPS: sudo systemctl restart cups Verify: lpstat -t 7. Configure CUPS Network Access The CUPS configuration is: /etc/cups/cupsd.conf The important server-side settings are: Port 631 Listen /run/cups/cups.sock Browsing On BrowseLocalProtocols dnssd WebInterface Yes Access for local network clients is allowed with: <Location /> Order allow,deny Allow @LOCAL </Location> CUPS should be listening on TCP port 631. Verify: sudo ss -ltnp | grep 631 Expected: 0.0.0.0:631 [::]:631 8. Fix the CUPS Hostname / Bad Request Issue Initially, clients could reach lux , but CUPS returned: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request and commands such as: lpstat -h lux.alfred.edu:631 -p returned: Error - add '/version=1.1' to server name. The actual issue was that CUPS was rejecting the HTTP Host: header for: lux.alfred.edu Edit: sudo nano /etc/cups/cupsd.conf Add near the top: ServerName lux.alfred.edu ServerAlias lux.alfred.edu For example: LogLevel warn ServerName lux.alfred.edu ServerAlias lux.alfred.edu PageLogFormat MaxLogSize 0 ErrorPolicy retry-job Port 631 Listen /run/cups/cups.sock Restart CUPS: sudo systemctl restart cups Clients should then be able to communicate normally with: lux.alfred.edu:631 9. Verify the Printer Is Shared On lux : sudo grep -A20 -B5 LabPrinter /etc/cups/printers.conf The LabPrinter section should contain: DeviceURI usb://Lexmark/MS310%20Series?serial=45147GLM3V8KL Accepting Yes Shared Yes The actual server configuration should remain: LabPrinter -> USB printer Do not change LabPrinter on lux to point back to: ipp://lux.alfred.edu:631/printers/LabPrinter That would create a loop where the print server points to itself. 10. Configure Lab Computers The controlled CASTLE Debian computers use lux as their central CUPS server. Current systems include: bedi.alfred.edu alan.alfred.edu ahmad.alfred.edu daniel.alfred.edu saron.alfred.edu dagim.alfred.edu garegin.alfred.edu kumar.alfred.edu Install the CUPS client if necessary: sudo apt install -y cups-client Create: /etc/cups/client.conf with: ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631 This can be done using: echo 'ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631' | sudo tee /etc/cups/client.conf After this, CUPS client programs send their requests directly to lux . 11. Disable Automatic Printer Discovery The Alfred University network contains other discoverable printers, including HP and Toshiba printers. Without disabling discovery, the lab computers may display printers such as: HP_LaserJet_400_M401dne_1398E3 TOSHIBA_e_STUDIO3525AC_15969935 LabPrinter_lux These may be automatically created by cups-browsed . Disable automatic printer discovery on each CASTLE machine: sudo systemctl disable --now cups-browsed After disabling it, verify: lpstat -p lpstat -d The desired output is: printer LabPrinter is idle system default destination: LabPrinter In practice, disabling cups-browsed caused the unwanted auto-discovered queues to disappear automatically. 12. Configure Multiple Lab Computers from lux Once the FreeIPA account admin has sudo privileges on the lab machines, the CUPS client configuration can be pushed from lux . Example: for h in bedi alan ahmad daniel saron dagim garegin kumar; do ssh -t admin@$h.alfred.edu \ "echo 'ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631' | sudo tee /etc/cups/client.conf" done This requires entering the FreeIPA password for SSH and sudo. To disable cups-browsed on all machines: for h in bedi alan ahmad daniel saron dagim garegin kumar; do ssh -t admin@$h.alfred.edu ' sudo systemctl disable --now cups-browsed lpstat -p lpstat -d ' done A machine that is powered off or unreachable may return: No route to host It can simply be configured later. 13. FreeIPA Administrative Sudo Access The FreeIPA account: admin was added to the existing FreeIPA group: admins From the FreeIPA server/container: ipa group-add-member admins --users=admin Verify: ipa group-show admins The admins group should list: admin 14. FreeIPA Sudo Rule A FreeIPA sudo rule was created so members of the admins group can administer CASTLE machines. Create the rule: ipa sudorule-add castle-admins \ --desc="Full sudo access for FreeIPA administrators" Add the admins group: ipa sudorule-add-user castle-admins --groups=admins Allow all commands: ipa sudorule-mod castle-admins --cmdcat=all Allow commands to run as any user: ipa sudorule-mod castle-admins --runasusercat=all Allow the rule on all FreeIPA hosts: ipa sudorule-mod castle-admins --hostcat=all Verify: ipa sudorule-show castle-admins --all Important fields should include: Enabled: True Host category: all Command category: all RunAs User category: all User Groups: admins 15. Refresh SSSD After Sudo Changes Some clients did not immediately receive the new FreeIPA sudo rule because SSSD had cached the old information. On the affected client, become local root: su Clear the SSSD cache: /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E Restart SSSD: systemctl restart sssd Then completely log out and log back in as: admin Verify group membership: id The output should include: admins labstudents Verify sudo: sudo -l Expected: User admin may run the following commands: (ALL) ALL Then: sudo whoami should return: root 16. Important Note About su vs sudo The local Linux root password is independent from FreeIPA. Therefore: su may require a local root password that is different on each machine. Once the FreeIPA castle-admins sudo rule is working, local root access is normally unnecessary. Use: ssh admin@machine.alfred.edu sudo command instead. 17. Testing a Client On any CASTLE workstation: lpstat -p Expected: printer LabPrinter is idle Check the default: lpstat -d Expected: system default destination: LabPrinter Test printing: echo "CASTLE printer test" | lp The complete path is: Debian workstation | | CUPS / IPP v lux.alfred.edu | | USB v Lexmark MS310/MS312 Series 18. Printing from GUI Applications Because LabPrinter is the system default printer, users should normally be able to open an application and press: Ctrl + P The print dialog should show: LabPrinter as the available/default printer. This applies to applications such as: Firefox / Chromium PDF viewers LibreOffice text editors other applications using the system print dialog 19. Current Desired Client State Each CASTLE lab machine should have: /etc/cups/client.conf containing: ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631 cups-browsed should be disabled: systemctl is-enabled cups-browsed Expected: disabled The printer check should return: lpstat -p lpstat -d Expected: printer LabPrinter is idle system default destination: LabPrinter 20. Current Desired Server State On lux : lpstat -v LabPrinter should return: device for LabPrinter: usb://Lexmark/MS310%20Series?serial=45147GLM3V8KL The printer must remain shared: Shared Yes The server must listen on port 631: sudo ss -ltnp | grep 631 and /etc/cups/cupsd.conf should include: ServerName lux.alfred.edu ServerAlias lux.alfred.edu Port 631 21. Troubleshooting lpinfo: command not found lpinfo is normally located in: /usr/sbin/lpinfo Use: sudo /usr/sbin/lpinfo -v IPP Everywhere driver requires an IPP connection This happens when attempting: -m everywhere against a USB printer. For the USB Lexmark on lux , use the Generic PostScript driver instead: -m drv:///sample.drv/generic.ppd Unable to create PPD: No IPP attributes Do not create an unnecessary local -m everywhere queue if the workstation is configured to use lux through: /etc/cups/client.conf The workstation can simply use the central CUPS server. HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request Make sure /etc/cups/cupsd.conf on lux contains: ServerName lux.alfred.edu ServerAlias lux.alfred.edu Then: sudo systemctl restart cups lpadmin: Forbidden If a workstation uses: ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631 then lpadmin may attempt to modify the CUPS configuration on lux . Remote printer administration is intentionally restricted. This does not indicate a printing problem. If: lpstat -d already returns: system default destination: LabPrinter nothing needs to be changed. Random HP/Toshiba Printers Appear Disable cups-browsed : sudo systemctl disable --now cups-browsed Then check: lpstat -p Only LabPrinter should remain. FreeIPA User Is in admins but Cannot Use sudo Clear the SSSD cache as local root: /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E systemctl restart sssd Log completely out, reconnect, then: sudo -l sudo whoami 22. New Machine Enrollment The final CASTLE enrollment script should automate: Fresh Debian installation | +--> Set hostname | +--> Install FreeIPA client | +--> Enroll into FreeIPA | +--> Configure SSSD | +--> Configure FreeIPA automount | +--> RAID/NFS roaming homes | +--> Configure /etc/cups/client.conf | +--> ServerName lux.alfred.edu:631 | +--> Disable cups-browsed | +--> Install CASTLE wallpaper | +--> Verify LabPrinter | └--> Reboot The custom deployment folder can contain: CASTLE-Setup/ ├── castle-enroll.sh └── castle-wallpaper.jpg After running the enrollment script and rebooting, a FreeIPA student should be able to: log in using their FreeIPA credentials; receive their RAID-backed roaming home directory; open a program and press Ctrl+P ; print using LabPrinter ; receive the CASTLE lab wallpaper. 23. Summary The final CASTLE printing design is: CASTLE LAB | +-----------------+-----------------+ | | | bedi alan ahmad | | | daniel saron dagim | | | garegin kumar ... \ | / \ | / +---------------+--------------+ | CUPS / IPP | v lux.alfred.edu | CUPS LabPrinter | USB | v Lexmark MS312dn Printer The CASTLE workstations rely on lux for the printer queue, while lux handles the physical USB connection to the Lexmark printer.

CASTLE Server Infrastructure This page describes how to set up and maintain services used in the CASTLE Lab. OS installation Install latest Debian(13) RAID install mdadm: sudo apt install mdadm Clear the old partition tables from the disks: sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme0n1 bs=4096 count=1000 sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme1n1 bs=4096 count=1000 sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme2n1 bs=4096 count=1000 Then create the RAID 5 array: sudo mdadm --create --verbose /dev/md0 --level=5 --raid-devices=3 /dev/nvme0n1 /dev/nvme1n1 /dev/nvme2n1 +Create a filesystem on your new RAID device: sudo mkfs.ext4 -F /dev/md0 Create a mount point and mount the drive: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid sudo mount /dev/md0 /mnt/raid Persist the configuration so it mounts automatically after a reboot: sudo mdadm --detail --scan | sudo tee -a /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf NFS,Roaming Home Directory This document describes the CASTLE Linux lab architecture for centralized authentication, RAID-backed student storage, NFS roaming home directories, FreeIPA automount, quotas, and automatic student-home provisioning. All deployment-specific and personally identifying information has been replaced with safe placeholders. The examples below use documentation-only values such as: Server FQDN: ipa01.example.test Domain: example.test Realm: EXAMPLE.TEST Server IP: 192.0.2.10 Student username: student01 Client IPs: 192.0.2.101, 192.0.2.102, ... example.test and 192.0.2.0/24 are placeholders only. 1. System Goal CASTLE allows a FreeIPA user to log into any configured Linux lab workstation and receive the same home directory and files. The basic architecture is: FreeIPA ipa01.example.test │ Authentication / UID / GID / home │ ▼ Lab workstation │ │ autofs + NFSv4 ▼ /home/students/<username> │ ▼ 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/<username> │ ▼ RAID5 The home directory is not copied between computers. Each workstation mounts the same centrally stored home directory from the server. This means files written on one workstation are immediately available from another workstation using the same user account. 2. Main Components CASTLE uses: FreeIPA Central authentication and identity SSSD Client-side identity lookup and FreeIPA integration autofs Automatic home-directory mounting NFSv4 Network filesystem transport Linux md RAID5 Centralized redundant storage ext4 RAID filesystem ext4 user quotas Storage limits per student systemd Automated RAID-home provisioning Podman FreeIPA server container 3. Example Server Layout Public documentation example: Host operating system: Debian 13 FreeIPA container OS: Rocky Linux 9 FreeIPA container: freeipa-server-container FreeIPA server: ipa01.example.test Domain: example.test Kerberos realm: EXAMPLE.TEST Storage server IP: 192.0.2.10 Replace these with private production values during deployment. 4. RAID Architecture CASTLE uses a Linux software RAID5 array: /dev/md0 It consists of three NVMe drives: /dev/nvme0n1 /dev/nvme1n1 /dev/nvme2n1 Conceptually: NVMe 1 ─┐ NVMe 2 ─┼── RAID5 ── /dev/md0 ── ext4 ── /mnt/raid NVMe 3 ─┘ RAID5 provides single-disk redundancy. RAID is not a backup. It does not protect against: accidental deletion administrator mistakes filesystem corruption malware multiple-disk failure loss of the server A separate backup system should still be used for important data. 5. Check RAID Health Basic status: cat /proc/mdstat Detailed status: sudo mdadm --detail /dev/md0 Device overview: lsblk -f A healthy RAID5 should show all expected member devices active. 6. Rebuilding RAID From Blank Drives This section is destructive. Do not run these commands on a working array containing data. Install mdadm : sudo apt update sudo apt install -y mdadm Create a three-disk RAID5: sudo mdadm --create /dev/md0 \ --level=5 \ --raid-devices=3 \ /dev/nvme0n1 \ /dev/nvme1n1 \ /dev/nvme2n1 Monitor RAID initialization: watch cat /proc/mdstat Create an ext4 filesystem: sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/md0 Get the new filesystem UUID: sudo blkid /dev/md0 A newly formatted RAID will have a new UUID. Do not copy a UUID from another system. 7. Mount the RAID Create the mount point: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid Example /etc/fstab entry: UUID=<RAID_FILESYSTEM_UUID> /mnt/raid ext4 defaults,nofail,discard,usrquota 0 2 Replace: <RAID_FILESYSTEM_UUID> with the actual value returned by: sudo blkid /dev/md0 Reload systemd and mount: sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo mount -a Verify: findmnt /mnt/raid df -h /mnt/raid 8. Enable User Quotas CASTLE uses filesystem quotas so one student cannot consume the entire RAID. Current policy: Soft limit: 4 GiB Hard limit: 5 GiB Install quota utilities: sudo apt update sudo apt install -y quota e2fsprogs Enable the ext4 internal user-quota feature: sudo tune2fs -Q usrquota /dev/md0 If a filesystem check is required: sudo umount /mnt/raid sudo e2fsck -f /dev/md0 sudo mount /mnt/raid Make sure /etc/fstab contains: usrquota Check quota enforcement: sudo quotaon -p /mnt/raid Desired state: user quota: on group quota: off project quota: off 9. ext4 Internal Quotas CASTLE uses ext4's internal quota inode. Inspect the filesystem: sudo tune2fs -l /dev/md0 The filesystem should show the quota feature and a user quota inode. An old-style file such as: /mnt/raid/aquota.user is not required. Do not run quotacheck simply to create aquota.user . 10. Quota Values The quota values passed to setquota are expressed in KiB: 4 GiB = 4194304 KiB 5 GiB = 5242880 KiB Apply a quota manually: sudo setquota -u <UID> 4194304 5242880 0 0 /mnt/raid Example using a fictional UID: sudo setquota -u 1001001 4194304 5242880 0 0 /mnt/raid View quotas: sudo repquota -s -n /mnt/raid 11. Student Storage Root All roaming student homes are stored under: /mnt/raid/homes Create it: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid/homes sudo chown root:root /mnt/raid/homes sudo chmod 0711 /mnt/raid/homes The parent directory uses: owner: root:root mode: 0711 Individual student homes use: owner: FreeIPA UID/GID mode: 0700 Example: /mnt/raid/homes/student01 should be owned by the numeric UID/GID assigned to student01 by FreeIPA. 12. Why /mnt/raid/homes Uses 0711 The parent directory: /mnt/raid/homes uses mode: 0711 This allows users to traverse the path to their own home while preventing ordinary users from listing the entire student-home directory. Each user's own directory uses: 0700 so other students cannot browse that user's files. 13. Install the NFS Server On the storage server: sudo apt update sudo apt install -y nfs-kernel-server nfs-common Enable NFS: sudo systemctl enable --now nfs-server Check: systemctl status nfs-server On Debian it may show: active (exited) while the kernel NFS services are functioning normally. Check port 2049: sudo ss -lntp | grep ':2049' Optional RPC inspection: rpcinfo -p 14. NFS Export File CASTLE uses: /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports rather than placing the configuration directly in /etc/exports . Example with several static workstation addresses: /mnt/raid/homes 192.0.2.101(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) 192.0.2.102(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) 192.0.2.103(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) Add every authorized CASTLE workstation using its privately assigned static address. Do not publish the production client IP list. 15. Reload NFS Exports After editing the file: sudo exportfs -rav Check the active configuration: sudo exportfs -v Check the service: systemctl is-active nfs-server Expected: active 16. NFS Options The current CASTLE export uses: rw sync no_subtree_check root_squash sec=sys rw allows students to write to their home directories. sync uses synchronous server-side NFS write behavior. no_subtree_check disables subtree checking. root_squash prevents root on a workstation from automatically becoming root on the NFS server. sec=sys uses UNIX numeric UID/GID credentials. Keep: root_squash enabled. Do not normally use: no_root_squash for student workstations. 17. Security Limitation of sec=sys With: sec=sys the NFS server trusts the UID/GID credentials provided by authorized client machines. FreeIPA ensures users receive consistent UID/GID values across the lab. Students therefore should not have unrestricted root or sudo access on the CASTLE workstations. A future hardening option is Kerberized NFS: sec=krb5p which provides stronger authentication and privacy. The current lab uses sec=sys . 18. Why Individual Static Addresses Are Used The NFS export is restricted to specific CASTLE workstations. The lab does not simply export storage to an entire building subnet. For example, this broad configuration is avoided: /mnt/raid/homes 192.0.2.0/24(...) Instead, only managed systems receive access: lab01 → static IP lab02 → static IP lab03 → static IP ... This reduces unnecessary exposure to unrelated devices on the same network. 19. Static Address Requirement The CASTLE NFS ACL is IP-based. Each workstation should therefore have a stable address assigned by the network administrators. The Linux machine can use either: manually configured static addressing or: DHCP reservation provided the workstation reliably receives the same address. FreeIPA authentication itself does not require the client IP to remain static. The static address is required here because of the NFS authorization design. 20. FreeIPA and DNS A FreeIPA host object can exist even if the corresponding hostname is not available through the organization's DNS infrastructure. For example, a client may have: host/lab01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST as a valid Kerberos principal without: lab01.example.test resolving through DNS. Because of this, CASTLE uses static IP addresses in the NFS export rather than client hostnames. The FreeIPA server itself must still be resolvable/reachable by clients. 21. FreeIPA Default Home Directory The default FreeIPA home-directory base is: /home/students The default shell is: /bin/bash Example configuration: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa config-mod \ --homedirectory=/home/students \ --defaultshell=/bin/bash ' Verify: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa config-show ' A new account such as: student01 should therefore receive: /home/students/student01 22. Why /home/students Is Used CASTLE intentionally does not replace the entire: /home directory. Roaming student accounts use: /home/students Local or special accounts may remain under paths such as: /home/localadmin /home/localguest This prevents CASTLE's autofs configuration from taking over every local home directory. 23. FreeIPA Automount Architecture CASTLE uses the FreeIPA automount location: default The layout is: auto.master /home/students → auto.students and: auto.students * → -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/& Replace: 192.0.2.10 with the private NFS server address. 24. Create auto.students Example: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e kinit admin ipa automountmap-show default auto.students >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa automountmap-add default auto.students ' Link it into auto.master : sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa automountkey-add default auto.master \ --key=/home/students \ --info=auto.students ' Add the wildcard: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa automountkey-add default auto.students \ --key="*" \ --info="-fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/&" ' If rebuilding an existing environment, inspect the keys first so duplicate entries are not added. 25. Critical Wildcard Detail The automount key must be exactly: * Do not store: \* The wildcard: * matches the requested subdirectory name. The: & in the NFS path is replaced with that value. Example: /home/students/student01 becomes: 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/student01 26. Check the Automount Configuration sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin echo "Automount maps:" ipa automountmap-find default echo echo "Master map:" ipa automountkey-find default auto.master echo echo "Student map:" ipa automountkey-find default auto.students ' Expected architecture: /home/students → auto.students and: * → -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard <SERVER_IP>:/mnt/raid/homes/& 27. CASTLE Student Group Create a FreeIPA group: labstudents Description: CASTLE lab students with roaming RAID home directories Create it: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa group-show labstudents >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa group-add labstudents \ --desc="CASTLE lab students with roaming RAID home directories" ' This group is used as the scope for automatic home provisioning. 28. FreeIPA Automember Rule Normal new students are automatically placed into: labstudents based on their FreeIPA home directory. Create the rule: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e kinit admin ipa automember-show labstudents --type=group >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa automember-add labstudents \ --type=group \ --desc="Automatically add users whose home is under /home/students" ipa automember-add-condition labstudents \ --type=group \ --key=homeDirectory \ --inclusive-regex="^/home/students/.*$" ' The rule matches users whose home looks like: /home/students/student01 29. Verify Automember sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin echo "Student group:" ipa group-show labstudents echo echo "Automember rule:" ipa automember-show labstudents \ --type=group \ --all ' Expected condition: homeDirectory=^/home/students/.*$ 30. Rebuild Membership for an Existing User If an existing user's home already matches the rule: ipa automember-rebuild --users=<USERNAME> Example: ipa automember-rebuild --users=student01 This is useful when introducing the rule after accounts already exist. 31. Manual Provisioning Tool CASTLE keeps a manual tool at: /usr/local/sbin/castle-home-add It is useful for: manual provisioning repairing an account migrating an older account troubleshooting automatic provisioning Normal use: sudo castle-home-add student01 Migration use: sudo castle-home-add --migrate student01 32. What castle-home-add Does The utility verifies: /mnt/raid is mounted user quotas are enabled FreeIPA is available the FreeIPA account exists the account has a valid UID and GID the home path matches /home/students/<username> It then: creates /mnt/raid/homes/<username> sets FreeIPA UID/GID ownership sets mode 0700 sets 4 GiB / 5 GiB quota verifies the result If an existing directory has unexpected ownership, the tool should refuse to silently take ownership of it. 33. Reliable Quota Check The quota test used by the CASTLE provisioning tools is: QUOTA_STATUS="$(quotaon -p "$RAID" 2>&1 || true)" if ! awk '/^user quota on / && / is on$/ {ok=1} END {exit ok ? 0 : 1}' <<< "$QUOTA_STATUS"; then echo "User quotas are not enabled on $RAID." echo "Current quota status:" printf '%s
' "$QUOTA_STATUS" exit 1 fi This prevents provisioning when quota enforcement is unexpectedly disabled. 34. Existing Account Migration Older accounts may have been configured with homes such as: /home/student01 instead of: /home/students/student01 Before migrating an established user: check the old local home copy any important local files confirm the user understands the migration Then run: sudo castle-home-add --migrate student01 Do not blindly migrate established accounts because mounting an NFS home can hide files that remain underneath the mount point. 35. Automatic Home Provisioning Normal new accounts are automatically provisioned. Workflow: Admin creates FreeIPA user │ ▼ FreeIPA assigns /home/students/<username> │ ▼ Automember adds user to labstudents │ ▼ castle-home-sync runs │ ▼ /mnt/raid/homes/<username> │ ├── correct UID/GID ├── mode 0700 └── quota 4 GiB / 5 GiB 36. Host-Keytab Authentication The automatic provisioning system does not store the FreeIPA administrator password. It uses the server host keytab. Example principal: host/ipa01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST Test access: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e export KRB5CCNAME=FILE:/tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache rm -f /tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache echo "Keytab principals:" klist -k /etc/krb5.keytab echo echo "Getting a temporary host ticket..." kinit -k \ -t /etc/krb5.keytab \ host/ipa01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST echo echo "Current ticket:" klist echo echo "Checking the student group:" ipa group-show labstudents --all rm -f /tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache ' Replace the example principal with the private deployment principal. Never publish the actual keytab. 37. Automatic Provisioning Script Path: /usr/local/sbin/castle-home-sync Recommended public-safe implementation: #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail RAID="/mnt/raid" HOME_ROOT="/mnt/raid/homes" IPA_CONTAINER="freeipa-server-container" IPA_GROUP="labstudents" # Replace with the real private host principal. IPA_HOST_PRINCIPAL="host/ipa01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST" # Values are in KiB. SOFT_QUOTA=4194304 HARD_QUOTA=5242880 if [[ $EUID -ne 0 ]]; then echo "This needs to run as root." exit 1 fi # Prevent timer and manual runs from overlapping. exec 9>/run/castle-home-sync.lock if ! flock -n 9; then echo "A CASTLE home sync is already running." exit 0 fi echo "CASTLE student home sync" echo "Started: $(date)" echo # Do not create directories if the RAID has failed to mount. if ! mountpoint -q "$RAID"; then echo "$RAID is not mounted. Stopping." exit 1 fi if ! podman container exists "$IPA_CONTAINER"; then echo "FreeIPA container '$IPA_CONTAINER' was not found." exit 1 fi if [[ "$(podman inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$IPA_CONTAINER")" != "true" ]]; then echo "FreeIPA container '$IPA_CONTAINER' is not running." exit 1 fi QUOTA_STATUS="$(quotaon -p "$RAID" 2>&1 || true)" if ! awk '/^user quota on / && / is on$/ {ok=1} END {exit ok ? 0 : 1}' <<< "$QUOTA_STATUS"; then echo "User quotas are not active on $RAID." printf '%s
' "$QUOTA_STATUS" exit 1 fi mkdir -p "$HOME_ROOT" chown root:root "$HOME_ROOT" chmod 0711 "$HOME_ROOT" echo "Reading members of '$IPA_GROUP'..." mapfile -t RECORDS < <( podman exec \ -e IPA_HOST_PRINCIPAL="$IPA_HOST_PRINCIPAL" \ "$IPA_CONTAINER" \ bash -lc ' set -euo pipefail export KRB5CCNAME="FILE:/tmp/castle-home-sync.ccache.$$" cleanup() { rm -f "$KRB5CCNAME" } trap cleanup EXIT kinit -k \ -t /etc/krb5.keytab \ "$IPA_HOST_PRINCIPAL" MEMBERS="$( ipa group-show labstudents | sed -n "s/^ Member users: //p" | tr "," "
" | sed "s/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//" | sed "/^$/d" )" for USERNAME in $MEMBERS; do DATA="$(ipa user-show "$USERNAME" --all --raw)" USER_UID="$( printf "%s
" "$DATA" | awk -F": " "/^[[:space:]]*uidnumber:/ {print \$2; exit}" )" USER_GID="$( printf "%s
" "$DATA" | awk -F": " "/^[[:space:]]*gidnumber:/ {print \$2; exit}" )" USER_HOME="$( printf "%s
" "$DATA" | awk -F": " "/^[[:space:]]*homedirectory:/ {print \$2; exit}" )" printf "%s	%s	%s	%s
" \ "$USERNAME" \ "$USER_UID" \ "$USER_GID" \ "$USER_HOME" done ' ) if [[ ${#RECORDS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "No users are currently in $IPA_GROUP." exit 0 fi echo "Found ${#RECORDS[@]} student account(s)." echo ERRORS=0 PROVISIONED=0 OK=0 for RECORD in "${RECORDS[@]}"; do IFS=$'	' read -r \ USERNAME USER_UID USER_GID USER_HOME \ <<< "$RECORD" echo "$USERNAME" if [[ ! "$USERNAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then echo " Username is not valid. Skipping." ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)) echo continue fi if [[ ! "$USER_UID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ || ! "$USER_GID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then echo " FreeIPA did not return a valid UID/GID." ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)) echo continue fi EXPECTED_HOME="/home/students/$USERNAME" RAID_HOME="$HOME_ROOT/$USERNAME" if [[ "$USER_HOME" != "$EXPECTED_HOME" ]]; then echo " Home is $USER_HOME, not $EXPECTED_HOME." echo " Leaving this account alone." echo continue fi if [[ -e "$RAID_HOME" ]]; then if [[ ! -d "$RAID_HOME" ]]; then echo " $RAID_HOME exists but is not a directory." ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)) echo continue fi CURRENT_OWNER="$(stat -c '%u:%g' "$RAID_HOME")" EXPECTED_OWNER="${USER_UID}:${USER_GID}" if [[ "$CURRENT_OWNER" != "$EXPECTED_OWNER" ]]; then echo " Existing home has unexpected ownership." echo " Current: $CURRENT_OWNER" echo " Expected: $EXPECTED_OWNER" echo " Leaving it untouched." ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)) echo continue fi chmod 0700 "$RAID_HOME" setquota -u "$USER_UID" \ "$SOFT_QUOTA" \ "$HARD_QUOTA" \ 0 \ 0 \ "$RAID" echo " Existing roaming home is OK." OK=$((OK + 1)) else install -d \ -m 0700 \ -o "$USER_UID" \ -g "$USER_GID" \ "$RAID_HOME" setquota -u "$USER_UID" \ "$SOFT_QUOTA" \ "$HARD_QUOTA" \ 0 \ 0 \ "$RAID" echo " Created $RAID_HOME" echo " Owner: $USER_UID:$USER_GID" echo " Quota: 4 GiB soft / 5 GiB hard" PROVISIONED=$((PROVISIONED + 1)) fi echo done echo "Sync finished." echo "Existing homes checked: $OK" echo "New homes created: $PROVISIONED" echo "Errors: $ERRORS" if (( ERRORS > 0 )); then exit 1 fi Install: sudo chmod 0755 /usr/local/sbin/castle-home-sync 38. systemd Service Create: /etc/systemd/system/castle-home-sync.service Contents: [Unit] Description=Synchronize CASTLE FreeIPA labstudents roaming homes After=network-online.target nfs-server.service Wants=network-online.target [Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/castle-home-sync User=root Group=root A successful oneshot service normally becomes: inactive (dead) after it finishes. That is expected. 39. systemd Timer Create: /etc/systemd/system/castle-home-sync.timer Contents: [Unit] Description=Periodically provision CASTLE roaming student homes [Timer] OnBootSec=10min OnUnitActiveSec=4h AccuracySec=5min Unit=castle-home-sync.service [Install] WantedBy=timers.target The job therefore runs approximately: 10 minutes after boot and then: every 4 hours This interval is appropriate for a small lab where accounts are not created continuously. 40. Enable Automatic Provisioning sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now castle-home-sync.timer Check: systemctl list-timers castle-home-sync.timer --no-pager Run immediately if needed: sudo systemctl start castle-home-sync.service Check logs: sudo journalctl \ -u castle-home-sync.service \ -n 100 \ --no-pager A healthy run should end with: Errors: 0 41. Normal Student Account Workflow Once CASTLE is deployed, the normal account workflow is: FreeIPA UI │ ▼ Create student │ ▼ /home/students/<username> │ ▼ Automember → labstudents │ ▼ castle-home-sync │ ▼ RAID home created automatically The administrator normally does not need to manually: add the user to labstudents create the RAID home set ownership set permissions set quota create an automount entry If immediate provisioning is required: sudo systemctl start castle-home-sync.service 42. Enrolling a New CASTLE Workstation Use this procedure when adding a new Linux workstation to CASTLE. Existing CASTLE workstations that were enrolled under the older configuration do not need to be removed from FreeIPA or re-enrolled. If roaming homes are already working on those machines, leave them as they are. Set the Workstation Hostname Before enrolling the workstation, configure its permanent hostname and network settings. Example: sudo hostnamectl set-hostname lab01.example.test Verify the hostname: hostname -f The result should be the workstation's intended fully qualified domain name: lab01.example.test Make sure the workstation can reach the FreeIPA server before continuing. Install the Required Packages Install the FreeIPA client along with the packages required for CASTLE roaming home directories: sudo apt update sudo apt install -y \ freeipa-client \ nfs-common \ autofs \ sssd-tools The packages provide: freeipa-client — FreeIPA enrollment and authentication nfs-common — NFS client support autofs — automatic mounting of roaming home directories sssd-tools — SSSD cache and troubleshooting utilities Enroll the Workstation in FreeIPA Enroll the workstation: sudo ipa-client-install \ --server=ipa01.example.test \ --domain=example.test \ --realm=EXAMPLE.TEST Replace the example server, domain, and realm with the private CASTLE deployment values. Important: Do Not Use --mkhomedir New CASTLE clients should not be enrolled with: --mkhomedir CASTLE no longer uses locally created student home directories. Student homes are stored centrally on the CASTLE storage server and mounted through NFS and autofs. The intended layout is: /home/students/<username> ↓ autofs ↓ NFS ↓ /mnt/raid/homes/<username> Using --mkhomedir on new machines is unnecessary and may create local home directories when CASTLE expects the user's home to come from the central NFS server. Verify FreeIPA Enrollment After enrollment, confirm that FreeIPA users can be resolved: getent passwd student01 Use a valid test account from the private CASTLE environment. The user's home directory should eventually appear as: /home/students/student01 At this point, FreeIPA authentication may already work, but the workstation still needs to be configured to retrieve the centralized automount maps. 43. Configure FreeIPA Automount After the workstation has successfully joined FreeIPA, configure FreeIPA automount support. Run: sudo ipa-client-automount \ --server=ipa01.example.test \ --location=default Replace ipa01.example.test with the private FreeIPA server hostname. The client must already be enrolled in FreeIPA before this command is run. This configures SSSD and autofs so the workstation can retrieve CASTLE's centrally managed automount maps from FreeIPA. Refresh SSSD and Autofs Clear cached FreeIPA information: sudo /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E || true Restart SSSD: sudo systemctl restart sssd Enable and start autofs: sudo systemctl enable --now autofs Restart autofs: sudo systemctl restart autofs Verify the Services Check SSSD: systemctl is-active sssd Expected: active Check autofs: systemctl is-active autofs Expected: active Verify the FreeIPA Automount Maps Display the automount maps received by the workstation: sudo /usr/sbin/automount -m The CASTLE configuration should include a mount point similar to: Mount point: /home/students instance type(s): sss map: auto.students The auto.students map should contain a wildcard entry similar to: * | -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard <NFS_SERVER_IP>:/mnt/raid/homes/& Replace <NFS_SERVER_IP> with the private address of the CASTLE NFS server. The wildcard allows one automount rule to handle every student. For example: /home/students/student01 maps to: <NFS_SERVER_IP>:/mnt/raid/homes/student01 Verify the User Home Directory Check a FreeIPA student account: getent passwd student01 The home-directory field should point to: /home/students/student01 If it still shows an older value such as: /home/student01 clear the SSSD cache and restart the services again: sudo /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E sudo systemctl restart sssd sudo systemctl restart autofs Then check again: getent passwd student01 Verify NFS Connectivity Confirm that the workstation can reach the CASTLE NFS server on TCP port 2049: timeout 3 bash -c '</dev/tcp/<NFS_SERVER_IP>/2049' If the command exits without an error, the NFS service is reachable. The workstation's static or reserved IP address must also be listed in the CASTLE NFS export ACL on the server. Test the Roaming Home Log into the workstation using a CASTLE student account. Check the user's home: echo "$HOME" Expected: /home/students/student01 Check the actual mount: findmnt -T "$HOME" The source should point to the CASTLE NFS server. Create a test file: echo "CASTLE roaming-home test from $(hostname)" > ~/castle-test.txt Verify it: cat ~/castle-test.txt Log into another configured CASTLE workstation with the same account and run: cat ~/castle-test.txt The file should appear immediately because both workstations are using the same NFS-backed home directory. After testing: rm -f ~/castle-test.txt 44. Legacy CASTLE Workstations Some CASTLE workstations may have originally been enrolled using the older command: sudo ipa-client-install \ --server=ipa01.example.test \ --domain=example.test \ --realm=EXAMPLE.TEST \ --mkhomedir These machines do not need to be removed from FreeIPA or re-enrolled simply because CASTLE later moved to centralized roaming home directories. If a legacy workstation already has: working FreeIPA authentication; nfs-common installed; autofs installed and running; SSSD retrieving the FreeIPA automount maps; access to the CASTLE NFS server; successful roaming-home tests; then leave the workstation enrolled as-is. For all new CASTLE workstations, use the current enrollment process without --mkhomedir . 45. New CASTLE Workstation Checklist A newly deployed CASTLE workstation should pass all of the following checks: [ ] Permanent hostname configured [ ] Correct static or reserved IP assigned [ ] FreeIPA server reachable [ ] freeipa-client installed [ ] nfs-common installed [ ] autofs installed [ ] sssd-tools installed [ ] Workstation enrolled in FreeIPA [ ] --mkhomedir was NOT used [ ] ipa-client-automount configured [ ] SSSD active [ ] autofs active [ ] /home/students automount map visible [ ] NFS server reachable on TCP 2049 [ ] Workstation IP authorized by the NFS server [ ] FreeIPA user's home is /home/students/<username> [ ] User can log in successfully [ ] Files created on one workstation appear on another 46. Expected Client Results A configured client should report: SSSD: active autofs: active getent passwd <username> should show: /home/students/<username> The automount map should include: Mount point: /home/students instance type(s): sss map: auto.students and a wildcard entry similar to: * | -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/& 47. SSSD Cache Refresh When a FreeIPA user attribute changes, clients may retain an older cached value. Clear the cache: sudo /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E Restart: sudo systemctl restart sssd sudo systemctl restart autofs Check the user again: getent passwd student01 48. /usr/sbin and Root Shells If root access is obtained with: su instead of: su - /usr/sbin may not be present in the shell's PATH . Using full paths avoids confusion: /usr/sbin/sss_cache /usr/sbin/automount 49. Verify NFS Connectivity From a client: timeout 3 bash -c '</dev/tcp/192.0.2.10/2049' If successful, TCP port 2049 is reachable. The server must also authorize that client's static IP in: /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports 50. End-to-End SSH Test A useful final test is to log into two different workstations using the same FreeIPA student account. From an administrator system: ssh student01@192.0.2.101 ' echo "Host: $(hostname)" echo "User: $(whoami)" echo "HOME: $HOME" findmnt -T "$HOME" || true echo "Created on $(hostname) at $(date)" > \ "$HOME/castle-roaming-test.txt" cat "$HOME/castle-roaming-test.txt" ' Then connect to another workstation: ssh student01@192.0.2.102 ' echo "Host: $(hostname)" echo "User: $(whoami)" echo "HOME: $HOME" findmnt -T "$HOME" || true cat "$HOME/castle-roaming-test.txt" ' The second workstation should immediately see the file created on the first. 51. Why Files Appear Immediately CASTLE is not syncing files between workstations. Both workstations are accessing: the same directory on the NFS server For example: workstation A: /home/students/student01 │ ▼ server: /mnt/raid/homes/student01 ▲ │ workstation B: /home/students/student01 Therefore no synchronization service or waiting period is needed. 52. Downloads, Documents, Desktop, Etc. Directories such as: Downloads Documents Desktop Pictures are normally stored inside the user's home. For example: /home/students/student01/Downloads actually resides on the server as: /mnt/raid/homes/student01/Downloads A file downloaded on one CASTLE workstation should therefore appear when the same user logs into another CASTLE workstation. Files saved outside the roaming home, such as: /tmp /local-storage another local disk do not automatically roam. 53. Verify a Home Mount While logged in as a student: echo "$HOME" Expected: /home/students/student01 Inspect the mount: findmnt -T "$HOME" The source should point to the central NFS server. 54. Test File Creation On one workstation: echo "CASTLE test from $(hostname)" > ~/castle-test.txt cat ~/castle-test.txt On another workstation using the same account: cat ~/castle-test.txt The contents should match immediately. 55. Cleaning Up Test Files Delete a test file from the user's session: rm -f ~/castle-test.txt Or from the server: sudo rm -f \ /mnt/raid/homes/student01/castle-test.txt Because it is the same centralized home, deleting it from the server removes it from every workstation. Be careful when deleting directly from /mnt/raid/homes . 56. Finding Known Test Files Before deleting multiple files, inspect them first: sudo find /mnt/raid/homes \ -maxdepth 2 \ -name 'castle-*-test.txt' \ -print Only delete files after verifying the output contains exactly what is intended. 57. NFS Export Backup Before Changes Before editing the NFS ACL: sudo cp \ /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports \ "/etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports.backup-$(date +%F-%H%M%S)" This creates a timestamped rollback copy. 58. Restore the Latest NFS Export Backup BACKUP="$( ls -1t /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports.backup-* \ 2>/dev/null | head -n1 )" if [[ -z "$BACKUP" ]]; then echo "No NFS export backup was found." exit 1 fi echo "Restoring $BACKUP" sudo cp \ "$BACKUP" \ /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports sudo exportfs -rav sudo exportfs -v 59. Server RAID Health Check echo "RAID status:" cat /proc/mdstat echo echo "Detailed array information:" sudo mdadm --detail /dev/md0 60. Filesystem Health Check echo "RAID mount:" findmnt /mnt/raid echo echo "Space:" df -h /mnt/raid echo echo "Filesystem:" sudo blkid /dev/md0 61. Quota Health Check echo "Quota status:" sudo quotaon -p /mnt/raid echo echo "Quota report:" sudo repquota -s -n /mnt/raid 62. Student Home Health Check sudo find /mnt/raid/homes \ -mindepth 1 \ -maxdepth 1 \ -type d \ -printf '%f UID=%U GID=%G MODE=%m
' | sort Each student directory should normally have: mode 700 and ownership matching the user's FreeIPA UID/GID. 63. NFS Health Check echo "NFS service:" systemctl is-active nfs-server echo echo "Active exports:" sudo exportfs -v echo echo "NFS listener:" sudo ss -lntp | grep ':2049' || true 64. Provisioning Health Check echo "CASTLE timer:" systemctl list-timers \ castle-home-sync.timer \ --no-pager echo echo "Recent provisioning log:" sudo journalctl \ -u castle-home-sync.service \ -n 50 \ --no-pager 65. FreeIPA CASTLE Health Check sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin echo "FreeIPA defaults:" ipa config-show | grep -E \ "Home directory base|Default shell|Default users group" echo echo "CASTLE student group:" ipa group-show labstudents echo echo "Automember rule:" ipa automember-show \ labstudents \ --type=group \ --all echo echo "Automount maps:" ipa automountmap-find default echo echo "Master map:" ipa automountkey-find \ default \ auto.master echo echo "Student map:" ipa automountkey-find \ default \ auto.students ' 66. Check One User End to End Example: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container \ ipa user-show student01 Expected home: /home/students/student01 Check storage: sudo stat \ -c 'Path=%n UID=%u GID=%g Mode=%a' \ /mnt/raid/homes/student01 Expected mode: 700 Check quota: sudo repquota -s -n /mnt/raid Expected policy: soft: 4096M hard: 5120M 67. Client Troubleshooting: Home Still Shows /home/<user> If: getent passwd student01 shows an old local-style home, clear SSSD: sudo /usr/sbin/sss_cache -E sudo systemctl restart sssd sudo systemctl restart autofs Check again: getent passwd student01 68. Client Troubleshooting: Automount Map Missing Run: sudo /usr/sbin/automount -m If /home/students is missing, verify: the machine is enrolled in FreeIPA ipa-client-automount has been configured SSSD is running autofs is running the FreeIPA automount location is "default" Configure automount if required: sudo ipa-client-automount \ --server=ipa01.example.test \ --location=default Then restart: sudo systemctl restart sssd sudo systemctl restart autofs 69. Client Troubleshooting: NFS Access Denied Check the client's IP: ip -4 addr Verify that exact address is listed in: /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports on the server. Then reload: sudo exportfs -rav Check: sudo exportfs -v 70. Client Troubleshooting: NFS Port Unreachable From the workstation: timeout 3 bash -c '</dev/tcp/192.0.2.10/2049' If it fails, check: routing VLAN assignment server reachability NFS service host firewall network firewall static IP configuration 71. Client Troubleshooting: Permission Denied as Root This can be normal. CASTLE uses: root_squash so root on a client is not treated as server root over NFS. Test access as the actual FreeIPA user instead. 72. Removing a Student Removing an account requires care because its RAID home may contain data. Do not automatically delete: /mnt/raid/homes/<username> just because the FreeIPA account is disabled or removed. Recommended process: disable account confirm retention requirements archive data if necessary remove RAID home only after approval clear quota if appropriate 73. Backups RAID5 is not sufficient protection for student files. Production deployments should consider backing up: /mnt/raid/homes to storage independent of the RAID server. The backup system should ideally protect against: accidental deletion filesystem corruption server loss multiple-drive failure ransomware 74. Security Notes The current security model includes: FreeIPA authentication central UID/GID assignment private 0700 home directories root_squash IP-restricted NFS exports no student sudo/root access quota enforcement host-keytab automation no stored FreeIPA admin password Potential future improvements include: Kerberized NFS using sec=krb5p host firewall rules for TCP 2049 off-server backups monitoring/alerting for RAID health monitoring failed provisioning runs 75. Sensitive Files That Must Never Be Published Do not commit any of the following to a public repository: /etc/krb5.keytab Kerberos credential caches admin passwords SSH private keys TLS private keys production /etc/hosts real /etc/exports client list real filesystem UUIDs if considered internal real DNS server addresses student account exports private network diagrams containing addresses 76. Public Documentation Placeholder Rules Use values such as: student01 student02 lab01.example.test ipa01.example.test 192.0.2.10 192.0.2.101 1001001 <RAID_FILESYSTEM_UUID> Never replace these with live internal identifiers in the public version. Keep real values in private operational documentation. 77. Normal Day-to-Day Administration Creating a student normally consists only of: FreeIPA UI ↓ Add user The account receives: /home/students/<username> Automember adds: labstudents The next automatic sync creates: /mnt/raid/homes/<username> with: FreeIPA UID/GID mode 0700 4 GiB soft quota 5 GiB hard quota No per-user automount configuration is required. 78. Immediate Provisioning If waiting for the four-hour timer is inconvenient: sudo systemctl start castle-home-sync.service Check: sudo journalctl \ -u castle-home-sync.service \ -n 50 \ --no-pager 79. Manual Recovery Provisioning For a normal account: sudo castle-home-add <username> For an old account requiring home migration: sudo castle-home-add --migrate <username> Only use --migrate after checking local files. 80. Full Rebuild Order If rebuilding CASTLE from an already functioning FreeIPA server: 1. Install mdadm 2. Build or assemble RAID5 3. Create ext4 filesystem 4. Enable ext4 user quota 5. Configure /etc/fstab 6. Mount /mnt/raid 7. Verify quota enforcement 8. Create /mnt/raid/homes 9. Install NFS server 10. Assign stable client addresses 11. Configure NFS client ACL 12. Reload NFS exports 13. Set FreeIPA home base to /home/students 14. Create auto.students 15. Link /home/students in auto.master 16. Add wildcard * automount rule 17. Create labstudents 18. Create Automember condition 19. Install castle-home-add 20. Verify server host-keytab read access 21. Install castle-home-sync 22. Install systemd service 23. Install systemd timer 24. Enable provisioning timer 25. Enroll client workstations in FreeIPA 26. Configure ipa-client-automount 27. Install nfs-common/autofs/sssd-tools 28. Restart SSSD and autofs 29. Verify automount map 30. Verify NFS connectivity 31. Test login 32. Create file on one workstation 33. Verify file immediately from another 34. Configure backups 81. Final Architecture FreeIPA ipa01.example.test │ ▼ User account │ /home/students │ ▼ labstudents │ Automember │ ▼ castle-home-sync │ ┌───────────┴───────────┐ ▼ ▼ /mnt/raid/homes/user quota │ 4G / 5G │ ▼ NFS server │ ▼ static client ACL │ ▼ CASTLE workstations │ SSSD + autofs │ ▼ /home/students/<username> 82. Expected User Experience A student can: log into workstation A download or create files log out log into workstation B see the same Downloads/Documents/Desktop/files because both systems access the same NFS-backed home directory. There is no file-copy or synchronization delay. 83. Final Operational State A completed CASTLE deployment should have: Healthy RAID5 Mounted ext4 filesystem User quotas enabled /mnt/raid/homes configured NFS server active Only approved static clients exported root_squash enabled FreeIPA authentication working /home/students as the student home base FreeIPA wildcard automount configured labstudents group configured Automember configured Automatic home provisioning enabled 4-hour systemd timer enabled FreeIPA clients enrolled FreeIPA automount configured on clients SSSD active autofs active NFS connectivity working roaming files confirmed across multiple clients At that point, normal new-user administration is reduced to creating the student account in FreeIPA.

docs.text: This page describes how to set up and maintain services used in the CASTLE Lab.
docs.title: CASTLE Server Infrastructure

docs.text: Install latest Debian(13)
docs.title: OS installation

docs.text: install mdadm: sudo apt install mdadm Clear the old partition tables from the disks: sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme0n1 bs=4096 count=1000 sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme1n1 bs=4096 count=1000 sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme2n1 bs=4096 count=1000 Then create the RAID 5 array: sudo mdadm --create --verbose /dev/md0 --level=5 --raid-devices=3 /dev/nvme0n1 /dev/nvme1n1 /dev/nvme2n1 +Create a filesystem on your new RAID device: sudo mkfs.ext4 -F /dev/md0 Create a mount point and mount the drive: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid sudo mount /dev/md0 /mnt/raid Persist the configuration so it mounts automatically after a reboot: sudo mdadm --detail --scan | sudo tee -a /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf
docs.title: RAID

docs.text: This document describes the CASTLE Linux lab architecture for centralized authentication, RAID-backed student storage, NFS roaming home directories, FreeIPA automount, quotas, and automatic student-home provisioning. All deployment-specific and personally identifying information has been replaced with safe placeholders. The examples below use documentation-only values such as: Server FQDN: ipa01.example.test Domain: example.test Realm: EXAMPLE.TEST Server IP: 192.0.2.10 Student username: student01 Client IPs: 192.0.2.101, 192.0.2.102, ... example.test and 192.0.2.0/24 are placeholders only.
docs.title: NFS,Roaming Home Directory

docs.text: CASTLE allows a FreeIPA user to log into any configured Linux lab workstation and receive the same home directory and files. The basic architecture is: FreeIPA ipa01.example.test │ Authentication / UID / GID / home │ ▼ Lab workstation │ │ autofs + NFSv4 ▼ /home/students/<username> │ ▼ 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/<username> │ ▼ RAID5 The home directory is not copied between computers. Each workstation mounts the same centrally stored home directory from the server. This means files written on one workstation are immediately available from another workstation using the same user account.
docs.title: 1. System Goal

docs.text: CASTLE uses: FreeIPA Central authentication and identity SSSD Client-side identity lookup and FreeIPA integration autofs Automatic home-directory mounting NFSv4 Network filesystem transport Linux md RAID5 Centralized redundant storage ext4 RAID filesystem ext4 user quotas Storage limits per student systemd Automated RAID-home provisioning Podman FreeIPA server container
docs.title: 2. Main Components

docs.text: Public documentation example: Host operating system: Debian 13 FreeIPA container OS: Rocky Linux 9 FreeIPA container: freeipa-server-container FreeIPA server: ipa01.example.test Domain: example.test Kerberos realm: EXAMPLE.TEST Storage server IP: 192.0.2.10 Replace these with private production values during deployment.
docs.title: 3. Example Server Layout

docs.text: CASTLE uses a Linux software RAID5 array: /dev/md0 It consists of three NVMe drives: /dev/nvme0n1 /dev/nvme1n1 /dev/nvme2n1 Conceptually: NVMe 1 ─┐ NVMe 2 ─┼── RAID5 ── /dev/md0 ── ext4 ── /mnt/raid NVMe 3 ─┘ RAID5 provides single-disk redundancy. RAID is not a backup. It does not protect against: accidental deletion administrator mistakes filesystem corruption malware multiple-disk failure loss of the server A separate backup system should still be used for important data.
docs.title: 4. RAID Architecture

docs.text: Basic status: cat /proc/mdstat Detailed status: sudo mdadm --detail /dev/md0 Device overview: lsblk -f A healthy RAID5 should show all expected member devices active.
docs.title: 5. Check RAID Health

docs.text: This section is destructive. Do not run these commands on a working array containing data. Install mdadm : sudo apt update sudo apt install -y mdadm Create a three-disk RAID5: sudo mdadm --create /dev/md0 \ --level=5 \ --raid-devices=3 \ /dev/nvme0n1 \ /dev/nvme1n1 \ /dev/nvme2n1 Monitor RAID initialization: watch cat /proc/mdstat Create an ext4 filesystem: sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/md0 Get the new filesystem UUID: sudo blkid /dev/md0 A newly formatted RAID will have a new UUID. Do not copy a UUID from another system.
docs.title: 6. Rebuilding RAID From Blank Drives

docs.text: Create the mount point: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid Example /etc/fstab entry: UUID=<RAID_FILESYSTEM_UUID> /mnt/raid ext4 defaults,nofail,discard,usrquota 0 2 Replace: <RAID_FILESYSTEM_UUID> with the actual value returned by: sudo blkid /dev/md0 Reload systemd and mount: sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo mount -a Verify: findmnt /mnt/raid df -h /mnt/raid
docs.title: 7. Mount the RAID

docs.text: CASTLE uses filesystem quotas so one student cannot consume the entire RAID. Current policy: Soft limit: 4 GiB Hard limit: 5 GiB Install quota utilities: sudo apt update sudo apt install -y quota e2fsprogs Enable the ext4 internal user-quota feature: sudo tune2fs -Q usrquota /dev/md0 If a filesystem check is required: sudo umount /mnt/raid sudo e2fsck -f /dev/md0 sudo mount /mnt/raid Make sure /etc/fstab contains: usrquota Check quota enforcement: sudo quotaon -p /mnt/raid Desired state: user quota: on group quota: off project quota: off
docs.title: 8. Enable User Quotas

docs.text: CASTLE uses ext4's internal quota inode. Inspect the filesystem: sudo tune2fs -l /dev/md0 The filesystem should show the quota feature and a user quota inode. An old-style file such as: /mnt/raid/aquota.user is not required. Do not run quotacheck simply to create aquota.user .
docs.title: 9. ext4 Internal Quotas

docs.text: The quota values passed to setquota are expressed in KiB: 4 GiB = 4194304 KiB 5 GiB = 5242880 KiB Apply a quota manually: sudo setquota -u <UID> 4194304 5242880 0 0 /mnt/raid Example using a fictional UID: sudo setquota -u 1001001 4194304 5242880 0 0 /mnt/raid View quotas: sudo repquota -s -n /mnt/raid
docs.title: 10. Quota Values

docs.text: All roaming student homes are stored under: /mnt/raid/homes Create it: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/raid/homes sudo chown root:root /mnt/raid/homes sudo chmod 0711 /mnt/raid/homes The parent directory uses: owner: root:root mode: 0711 Individual student homes use: owner: FreeIPA UID/GID mode: 0700 Example: /mnt/raid/homes/student01 should be owned by the numeric UID/GID assigned to student01 by FreeIPA.
docs.title: 11. Student Storage Root

docs.text: The parent directory: /mnt/raid/homes uses mode: 0711 This allows users to traverse the path to their own home while preventing ordinary users from listing the entire student-home directory. Each user's own directory uses: 0700 so other students cannot browse that user's files.
docs.title: 12. Why /mnt/raid/homes Uses 0711

docs.text: On the storage server: sudo apt update sudo apt install -y nfs-kernel-server nfs-common Enable NFS: sudo systemctl enable --now nfs-server Check: systemctl status nfs-server On Debian it may show: active (exited) while the kernel NFS services are functioning normally. Check port 2049: sudo ss -lntp | grep ':2049' Optional RPC inspection: rpcinfo -p
docs.title: 13. Install the NFS Server

docs.text: CASTLE uses: /etc/exports.d/castle-homes.exports rather than placing the configuration directly in /etc/exports . Example with several static workstation addresses: /mnt/raid/homes 192.0.2.101(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) 192.0.2.102(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) 192.0.2.103(rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash,sec=sys) Add every authorized CASTLE workstation using its privately assigned static address. Do not publish the production client IP list.
docs.title: 14. NFS Export File

docs.text: After editing the file: sudo exportfs -rav Check the active configuration: sudo exportfs -v Check the service: systemctl is-active nfs-server Expected: active
docs.title: 15. Reload NFS Exports

docs.text: The current CASTLE export uses: rw sync no_subtree_check root_squash sec=sys rw allows students to write to their home directories. sync uses synchronous server-side NFS write behavior. no_subtree_check disables subtree checking. root_squash prevents root on a workstation from automatically becoming root on the NFS server. sec=sys uses UNIX numeric UID/GID credentials. Keep: root_squash enabled. Do not normally use: no_root_squash for student workstations.
docs.title: 16. NFS Options

docs.text: With: sec=sys the NFS server trusts the UID/GID credentials provided by authorized client machines. FreeIPA ensures users receive consistent UID/GID values across the lab. Students therefore should not have unrestricted root or sudo access on the CASTLE workstations. A future hardening option is Kerberized NFS: sec=krb5p which provides stronger authentication and privacy. The current lab uses sec=sys .
docs.title: 17. Security Limitation of sec=sys

docs.text: The NFS export is restricted to specific CASTLE workstations. The lab does not simply export storage to an entire building subnet. For example, this broad configuration is avoided: /mnt/raid/homes 192.0.2.0/24(...) Instead, only managed systems receive access: lab01 → static IP lab02 → static IP lab03 → static IP ... This reduces unnecessary exposure to unrelated devices on the same network.
docs.title: 18. Why Individual Static Addresses Are Used

docs.text: The CASTLE NFS ACL is IP-based. Each workstation should therefore have a stable address assigned by the network administrators. The Linux machine can use either: manually configured static addressing or: DHCP reservation provided the workstation reliably receives the same address. FreeIPA authentication itself does not require the client IP to remain static. The static address is required here because of the NFS authorization design.
docs.title: 19. Static Address Requirement

docs.text: A FreeIPA host object can exist even if the corresponding hostname is not available through the organization's DNS infrastructure. For example, a client may have: host/lab01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST as a valid Kerberos principal without: lab01.example.test resolving through DNS. Because of this, CASTLE uses static IP addresses in the NFS export rather than client hostnames. The FreeIPA server itself must still be resolvable/reachable by clients.
docs.title: 20. FreeIPA and DNS

docs.text: The default FreeIPA home-directory base is: /home/students The default shell is: /bin/bash Example configuration: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa config-mod \ --homedirectory=/home/students \ --defaultshell=/bin/bash ' Verify: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa config-show ' A new account such as: student01 should therefore receive: /home/students/student01
docs.title: 21. FreeIPA Default Home Directory

docs.text: CASTLE intentionally does not replace the entire: /home directory. Roaming student accounts use: /home/students Local or special accounts may remain under paths such as: /home/localadmin /home/localguest This prevents CASTLE's autofs configuration from taking over every local home directory.
docs.title: 22. Why /home/students Is Used

docs.text: CASTLE uses the FreeIPA automount location: default The layout is: auto.master /home/students → auto.students and: auto.students * → -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/& Replace: 192.0.2.10 with the private NFS server address.
docs.title: 23. FreeIPA Automount Architecture

docs.text: Example: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e kinit admin ipa automountmap-show default auto.students >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa automountmap-add default auto.students ' Link it into auto.master : sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa automountkey-add default auto.master \ --key=/home/students \ --info=auto.students ' Add the wildcard: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa automountkey-add default auto.students \ --key="*" \ --info="-fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/&" ' If rebuilding an existing environment, inspect the keys first so duplicate entries are not added.
docs.title: 24. Create auto.students

docs.text: The automount key must be exactly: * Do not store: \* The wildcard: * matches the requested subdirectory name. The: & in the NFS path is replaced with that value. Example: /home/students/student01 becomes: 192.0.2.10:/mnt/raid/homes/student01
docs.title: 25. Critical Wildcard Detail

docs.text: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin echo "Automount maps:" ipa automountmap-find default echo echo "Master map:" ipa automountkey-find default auto.master echo echo "Student map:" ipa automountkey-find default auto.students ' Expected architecture: /home/students → auto.students and: * → -fstype=nfs4,vers=4.2,rw,hard <SERVER_IP>:/mnt/raid/homes/&
docs.title: 26. Check the Automount Configuration

docs.text: Create a FreeIPA group: labstudents Description: CASTLE lab students with roaming RAID home directories Create it: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin ipa group-show labstudents >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa group-add labstudents \ --desc="CASTLE lab students with roaming RAID home directories" ' This group is used as the scope for automatic home provisioning.
docs.title: 27. CASTLE Student Group

docs.text: Normal new students are automatically placed into: labstudents based on their FreeIPA home directory. Create the rule: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e kinit admin ipa automember-show labstudents --type=group >/dev/null 2>&1 || \ ipa automember-add labstudents \ --type=group \ --desc="Automatically add users whose home is under /home/students" ipa automember-add-condition labstudents \ --type=group \ --key=homeDirectory \ --inclusive-regex="^/home/students/.*$" ' The rule matches users whose home looks like: /home/students/student01
docs.title: 28. FreeIPA Automember Rule

docs.text: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' kinit admin echo "Student group:" ipa group-show labstudents echo echo "Automember rule:" ipa automember-show labstudents \ --type=group \ --all ' Expected condition: homeDirectory=^/home/students/.*$
docs.title: 29. Verify Automember

docs.text: If an existing user's home already matches the rule: ipa automember-rebuild --users=<USERNAME> Example: ipa automember-rebuild --users=student01 This is useful when introducing the rule after accounts already exist.
docs.title: 30. Rebuild Membership for an Existing User

docs.text: CASTLE keeps a manual tool at: /usr/local/sbin/castle-home-add It is useful for: manual provisioning repairing an account migrating an older account troubleshooting automatic provisioning Normal use: sudo castle-home-add student01 Migration use: sudo castle-home-add --migrate student01
docs.title: 31. Manual Provisioning Tool

docs.text: The utility verifies: /mnt/raid is mounted user quotas are enabled FreeIPA is available the FreeIPA account exists the account has a valid UID and GID the home path matches /home/students/<username> It then: creates /mnt/raid/homes/<username> sets FreeIPA UID/GID ownership sets mode 0700 sets 4 GiB / 5 GiB quota verifies the result If an existing directory has unexpected ownership, the tool should refuse to silently take ownership of it.
docs.title: 32. What castle-home-add Does

docs.text: The quota test used by the CASTLE provisioning tools is: QUOTA_STATUS="$(quotaon -p "$RAID" 2>&1 || true)" if ! awk '/^user quota on / && / is on$/ {ok=1} END {exit ok ? 0 : 1}' <<< "$QUOTA_STATUS"; then echo "User quotas are not enabled on $RAID." echo "Current quota status:" printf '%s\n' "$QUOTA_STATUS" exit 1 fi This prevents provisioning when quota enforcement is unexpectedly disabled.
docs.title: 33. Reliable Quota Check

docs.text: Older accounts may have been configured with homes such as: /home/student01 instead of: /home/students/student01 Before migrating an established user: check the old local home copy any important local files confirm the user understands the migration Then run: sudo castle-home-add --migrate student01 Do not blindly migrate established accounts because mounting an NFS home can hide files that remain underneath the mount point.
docs.title: 34. Existing Account Migration

docs.text: Normal new accounts are automatically provisioned. Workflow: Admin creates FreeIPA user │ ▼ FreeIPA assigns /home/students/<username> │ ▼ Automember adds user to labstudents │ ▼ castle-home-sync runs │ ▼ /mnt/raid/homes/<username> │ ├── correct UID/GID ├── mode 0700 └── quota 4 GiB / 5 GiB
docs.title: 35. Automatic Home Provisioning

docs.text: The automatic provisioning system does not store the FreeIPA administrator password. It uses the server host keytab. Example principal: host/ipa01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST Test access: sudo podman exec -it freeipa-server-container bash -lc ' set -e export KRB5CCNAME=FILE:/tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache rm -f /tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache echo "Keytab principals:" klist -k /etc/krb5.keytab echo echo "Getting a temporary host ticket..." kinit -k \ -t /etc/krb5.keytab \ host/ipa01.example.test@EXAMPLE.TEST echo echo "Current ticket:" klist echo echo "Checking the student group:" ipa group-show labstudents --all rm -f /tmp/castle-provisioner-test.ccache ' Replace the example principal with the private deployment principal. Never publish the actual keytab.
